questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Lightly tap the brakes when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front of the car in line with the rear and straightens out the car.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: To merge safely, find a gap that is large enough for your car. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden and unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for drivers making sudden or unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is move out of their way.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey instructions from school crossing guards when near a school.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: In Arkansas, shared center lanes can be used:

options.text: To turn left.
To merge into a traffic lane after turning left.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A shared center turn lane has solid yellow lines on each side with a dashed yellow line. These lanes can be used by drivers turning left from either direction. In Arkansas, a vehicle turning left from a street or driveway can use the center lane to merge into traffic. Do not use the center lane to speed up.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop until all children have left the bus.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised before you go. Also check that no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: In rainy weather, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars on the road mixes with rain and makes the pavement slippery.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no vehicle from either direction can cross the center line to pass.

questions.question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the way is clear. This applies whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: Where are trucks' blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left of the cab.
Both on the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are much larger than car blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare. This makes it harder to see. Many vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to get back to your lane fast. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When passing on the left of a vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into the right lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to make a right turn, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with its red lights flashing must remain stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped. Do not move until the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus starts moving again.

questions.question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice and snow can lock the front wheels. When this happens, you lose steering control. To avoid hard braking, slow down before you reach icy or snowy areas.

questions.question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.
Increase the volume of your radio.
Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk and in rain or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:

options.text: Up the instrumental panel lights.
On your parking lights.
On your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: On your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Use low beam headlights whenever you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving isn't impaired.
Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely to things on the road. Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: In order to see potential hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In order to see potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for fast changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane cannot go in the direction shown by the arrow. You must stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.
